chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Hajjaj al-Khashshab said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who was traveling, and when he entered the city, he brought with him two witnesses. When his wife met him at the door, he made them witness his divorce from her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'A divorce does not take effect upon her.'
ai.seo_question: Does a divorce take effect if a husband declares it to his wife upon returning from travel with two witnesses?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a divorce declared upon a husband's return from travel, witnessed by two people, does not take effect, emphasizing the necessity of proper conditions and intent. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that mere declaration without the requisite legal framework or specific contextual triggers may not constitute a valid *talaq*. It serves as a critical precedent for understanding the procedural rigor required in marital dissolution within the Imami school.
